content: COBS (Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing) removes all zero bytes from a payload so a single zero byte can be used as an unambiguous frame delimiter; worst-case overhead is ceil(n/254) bytes, ~0.4% for typical payloads. Its key property for lossy links: after any corruption, the decoder resynchronizes automatically at the next zero-delimiter, needing no higher-layer recovery. COBS provides no error detection itself, so it is always paired with a CRC inside the frame. Used in production by Cyphal (aerospace/drone/robotics) over UART/RS-232/USB serial.
